messages:
sasha: heads-up — apiserver returning 503s in us-west2 starting ~09:14 UTC. Correlates with a huge burst of GPU attach ops from gpu-provisioner. etcd commit latency jumped to ~1.2s and controller-manager leader flipped twice. Anyone on call?

javier: saw it too. prometheus shows etcd fsync and commit latency spiking. apiserver request latencies P95/P99 climbed. pulling logs now.

javier: logs snippet:
```
E0403 09:14:21.123 kube-apiserver main.go: HTTP/1.1 503 POST /api/v1/nodes/provision/attach  (remote=10.20.30.5)
etcdserver: apply entries error: mvcc: required revision not found
controller-manager: error updating lease: context deadline exceeded
```

priya: CI burst from the new perf-tests enqueued ~1.2k attach requests in 3m to the same zone. Our provisioner has a high default concurrency and does parallel attach which blows past control-plane QPS.

anna: mitigation idea: pause the offending CI workflow and throttle the provisioner. Also consider switching attach to async webhook so apiserver doesn't block on the slow path.

leo: immediate steps I pushed: reduce gpu-provisioner concurrency to 10, toggle parallel_attach=false on instance-controller, and bump kube-apiserver flags: --max-requests-inflight=600 --max-mutating-requests-inflight=200 while we stabilize.

javier: note that increasing inflight helps surface errors slower but it increases etcd pressure. prefer throttling attach at source.

ops-bot: deploy gpu-provisioner v3.4.2 started at 09:18 UTC with concurrency=10 (rollout id: r-20260423-09-18).

priya: after throttling, observed: apiserver 5xxs dropped to ~0 in 10m, etcd commit latency back down to ~180ms, controller-manager leader stable. Looks contained.

anna: follow-ups for postmortem: add a token bucket rate limiter in gpu-provisioner, add canary gating for CI that does bulk attach, schedule an immediate etcd compaction and check NVMe IOPS on etcd nodes for sustained bursts. Also validate kube-controller-manager leader-elect lease/timeouts to avoid rapid flips under transient latencies.

leo: filing incident and cost-impact analysis. tagging owners in the doc: @priya @javier @anna

javier: incident created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0423-attach-surge — will capture timeline, graphs, and remediation actions.

sasha: thanks all. leaving notes in runbook about "attach burst" mitigation and adding an automated gate to pause mass attaches if apiserver 5xx > 5% in 2m. :thumbsup:
